02 / COMPARE WHAT CAN BE LEARNED

Five hypotheses. No pretend customers.
Demand tests: plans only

The smallest falsifiable tests below use fictional artifacts and a future format choice—not landing pages, paid traffic or invented sales. They are low-scope proposals, not proven global cost minima. 01 / OFFLINE FILE UTILITIES
Ledgerleaf Tools

Explain small CSV import problems

lf-schema direction · synthetic / unvalidated
SMALLEST OFFERING
A local CSV preflight with record, line and column findings; paste or select a UTF-8 file and download a value-free JSON report.
FROZEN STARTING ESTIMATE · NOT MEASURED
150 delivery + 30 test-preparation minutes. One strict CSV parser, a small finding contract and a local report; no import integrations, repairs, accounting or downstream export product.
OFFLINE DEPENDENCY
A fictional CSV fixture and a stable record/code contract. Seed fixture is available; the original checker in this demo has automated artifact tests. Neither establishes demand.
AUDIENCE HYPOTHESIS
People preparing a small CSV import; no such people have been recruited.
CHEAPEST SCOPED DEMAND QUESTION
Will a prospective user choose this checker over manual inspection for a second fictional import?
FUTURE TEST · NOT PERFORMED
After separate owner approval and consent, offer three prospective users a five-record fictional CSV and the checker. Ask each to explain a duplicate finding without coaching, then let them choose checker or plain text for a second sample. Estimated later observation/review: 45 founder minutes, plus unknown recruitment. Not funded this week.
PRECOMMITTED PASS RULE
At least 2 of 3 choose the checker again AND correctly identify the duplicate within five minutes.
DISCONFIRM / STOP
Park or simplify if fewer than 2 of 3 meet both conditions, or if explaining the checker takes longer than manual inspection.
WHAT A PASS CANNOT ESTABLISH
A tiny convenience sample could disconfirm utility; even a pass is not paying demand, retention or product-market fit.
Two original uncertainty rows + explicit non-goals
02 / PRACTICAL REFERENCE PUBLISHING
Fieldnote Guides

Make a supply-drawer reset easier to start

fn-outline direction · synthetic / unvalidated
SMALLEST OFFERING
A printable count, group, label, return and undo guide for a fictional supply drawer.
FROZEN STARTING ESTIMATE · NOT MEASURED
60 delivery + 25 test-preparation minutes. One page using 12 index cards, 3 binder clips, 2 empty envelopes and removable labels, with an undo step; no catalog or physical observation.
OFFLINE DEPENDENCY
Fictional inventory and a one-page comprehension rubric. The seed supplies the inventory. The proposed guide and rubric remain unbuilt.
AUDIENCE HYPOTHESIS
People who postpone organizing a shared supply drawer; unmeasured.
CHEAPEST SCOPED DEMAND QUESTION
Does someone choose and start using the guide instead of a plain list?
FUTURE TEST · NOT PERFORMED
With later owner approval and consent, offer three people a fictional inventory, a plain list and the guide. Ask them to pick a format and state their first grouping and reversal step in five minutes. Estimated later observation/review: 30 founder minutes, plus unknown recruitment. Not funded this week.
PRECOMMITTED PASS RULE
At least 2 of 3 choose the guide and can state a first action and how to undo it without another page.
DISCONFIRM / STOP
Park if fewer than 2 of 3 meet the rule, or setup takes more work than the plain list.
WHAT A PASS CANNOT ESTABLISH
Format choice and comprehension are weak utility signals, not purchases.
Two original uncertainty rows + explicit non-goals
03 / ACCESSIBLE OFFICE TEMPLATES
Quietbench Templates

Make purchasing requests easier to understand

qb-keyboard direction · synthetic / unvalidated
SMALLEST OFFERING
A printable purchasing request with item, reason, alternatives, hypothetical cost, needed-by window and reviewer question.
FROZEN STARTING ESTIMATE · NOT MEASURED
100 delivery + 35 test-preparation minutes. One request form with required/optional labels, a keyboard pass and print reading order; not a three-template catalog or accessibility certification.
OFFLINE DEPENDENCY
Plain-language field order and a keyboard/print review plan. The seed lists fields. A review plan can be drafted locally; the form and human review remain unperformed.
AUDIENCE HYPOTHESIS
People drafting small purchasing requests; unmeasured.
CHEAPEST SCOPED DEMAND QUESTION
Would a drafter choose this form over a blank note for a second fictional request?
FUTURE TEST · NOT PERFORMED
After approval and consent, ask three prospective drafters to navigate a fictional request using only a keyboard, explain which purpose field is required, then choose form or note for another request. Estimated later observation/review: 45 founder minutes, plus unknown recruitment. Not funded this week.
PRECOMMITTED PASS RULE
At least 2 of 3 finish without coaching, identify required purpose and choose the form again; no keyboard blocker is acceptable.
DISCONFIRM / STOP
Revise for any keyboard blocker; otherwise park if fewer than 2 of 3 meet the rule.
WHAT A PASS CANNOT ESTABLISH
A small walkthrough is neither an accessibility audit nor adoption evidence.
Two original uncertainty rows + explicit non-goals
04 / PRINTABLE CATEGORY PLANNERS
Routepaper Planners

Group errands without location tracking

rp-sheet direction · synthetic / unvalidated
SMALLEST OFFERING
A printable, location-free category grouping sheet for three fictional errands.
FROZEN STARTING ESTIMATE · NOT MEASURED
50 delivery + 20 test-preparation minutes. One category/time-window/can-wait/done sheet for a library return, labels and a fictional tote drop; no navigation or interviews.
OFFLINE DEPENDENCY
Fictional errands and an address-free grouping rule. Seed examples exist. The sheet is only a proposed alternative in this demo.
AUDIENCE HYPOTHESIS
People planning errands who do not need maps; unmeasured.
CHEAPEST SCOPED DEMAND QUESTION
Will someone choose the grouped sheet over a plain list, and does it change a decision?
FUTURE TEST · NOT PERFORMED
After approval and consent, give three people the same fictional errands in plain-list and grouped-sheet versions. Ask them to choose one and explain a grouping or deferral decision without adding any addresses. Estimated later observation/review: 30 founder minutes, plus unknown recruitment. Not funded this week.
PRECOMMITTED PASS RULE
At least 2 of 3 choose the sheet and identify one changed planning decision, without requesting locations.
DISCONFIRM / STOP
Park if grouping changes no decision, takes more effort than a list, or requires addresses.
WHAT A PASS CANNOT ESTABLISH
This is a low-scope interest test, not proof of repeat use or sales.
Two original uncertainty rows + explicit non-goals
05 / OFFLINE MICRO-LESSONS
Tinylesson Studio

Teach transferable file-naming habits

tl-sample direction · synthetic / unvalidated
SMALLEST OFFERING
An offline lesson on stable purpose and sortable dates, followed by an unrelated file-naming exercise.
FROZEN STARTING ESTIMATE · NOT MEASURED
110 delivery + 35 test-preparation minutes. One six-minute lesson, three fictional names and a transfer answer rubric; no course platform or observed learning gains.
OFFLINE DEPENDENCY
Original sample names and a transfer-scoring rubric. Seed naming examples exist. The lesson and transfer exercise remain proposed.
AUDIENCE HYPOTHESIS
People uncertain about file naming; unmeasured.
CHEAPEST SCOPED DEMAND QUESTION
Will a learner choose another short exercise after independently transferring the idea?
FUTURE TEST · NOT PERFORMED
After approval and consent, give three people a six-minute lesson using fictional filenames, then an unrelated naming exercise with a purpose/date rubric. Offer another exercise or an exit. Estimated later observation/review: 40 founder minutes, plus unknown recruitment. Not funded this week.
PRECOMMITTED PASS RULE
At least 2 of 3 meet the purpose/date rubric on the new example without copying and voluntarily choose another exercise.
DISCONFIRM / STOP
Park if fewer than 2 of 3 meet both conditions, copying substitutes for transfer, or exercise and feedback exceed six minutes.
WHAT A PASS CANNOT ESTABLISH
No causal learning gain or willingness to pay can be inferred from this tiny test.
Two original uncertainty rows + explicit non-goals

03 / A REAL, SMALL OFFERING

Ledgerleaf CSV Preflight
Built here · original code

Catch structural problems before a small import. This checker runs entirely in this page: no upload, accounts, storage or formula execution. It identifies records, not financial truth. Use fictional data for this demonstration; do not use real financial files.

Value-free JSON report

Header is record 1. Physical line is also reported, so quoted multiline fields remain locatable. The synthetic sample intentionally repeats its key at record 5. Formula-like checks are conservative and may flag ordinary negative numbers.

04 / KEEP THE OPTION VALUE

Build once. Reuse without pretending.
Reusable assets and venture-specific work still needed
Venture	Reusable asset / proposed use	What reuse cannot prove
Ledgerleaf Tools	Own the value-free finding schema, parser, fixture patterns and offline report UI.	The other ventures can reuse components, not inherit evidence of customer demand.
Fieldnote Guides	Use CSV checks for a fictional drawer-inventory table; reuse printable finding labels and the pass/stop test template.	A CSV parser does not write a useful guide; the original page and comprehension work are still needed.
Quietbench Templates	Reuse labeled controls, text-only finding codes and required-column checks on fictional request exports.	The checker cannot certify accessibility or whether a purchasing request is justified.
Routepaper Planners	Reuse the local-file pattern and required-column checks for category, time-window, can-wait and done.	Do not introduce location collection just because the parser accepts arbitrary text.
Tinylesson Studio	Turn fictional CSV failures into original data-hygiene exercises with stable, machine-checkable finding codes.	Automated check results are answer rubrics, not evidence that a learner improved.

05 / SHOW THE BOUNDARY

A new timebox. An intact evidence trail.
The seed is not a five-hour plan

This explicit user extension has 300 minutes total, at most one active unit, a new 30-minute reserve and 30-minute review. It authorizes $0 of spending. The old 480-minute reserve is itself infeasible here.

The narrower estimates do not assert that an eight-hour experiment takes 150 minutes. The deliverable changed. The full original candidate list remains frozen below.

A1Clock, not a timestamp

Integer model minutes, continuous working time, no nights, shifts, outages, or observed clocks. Paced arrivals are 10 minutes apart; stress arrivals are simultaneous.

A2Capacity, not headcount evidence

Baseline and triage: one slot each at intake, billing, seller-data, tax-data, credit, commercial, account, and disposition (8 total). Pod: intake/billing/disposition one each and pod two (5 total). Slots are nonpreemptive service capacity, not measured FTE or labor cost.

Baseline intake/validation/recheck/disposition = 6/18/10/12 min. Triage = 12/6/6/12. Pod = 6/10/10/12. Specialist minutes: PO 24, tax 30, quantity 24, account 30, credit 36, discount 24, terms 24. Pod exception service is 1.5×. Stress multipliers apply equally across designs.

A4FIFO with explicit ties

No random generator or priority cherry-picking. Complete all tasks at a timestamp in scheduling order, then process arrivals in quote-ID order, then dispatch FIFO by enqueue sequence. Resources dispatch in ID order; lowest free slot first. Intervals are [start, end).

A5Rework is a failed unchanged-input return

One tiny fixed workload, no stochastic confidence interval. Nearest-rank p50/p95; with eight cases p95 equals the maximum. Monetary calculations test source reconciliation only. No time-to-money conversion, realized savings, production integration, or adoption is measured.
